pricing.rule: Each delivered call bills price_usd × 1.15 + $0.005. A pending/async ack or an unverifiable charged call (delivered:false, refundable:false) bills price_usd × 1.15 with no per-call fee; refunded calls, in-batch duplicates and failed runs bill $0. A call runs only when its full delivered amount fits the batch's remaining max_usd, so max_usd must be at least Σ(price_usd × 1.15 + $0.005).

That in itself is extremely valuable, but at the same time I think for the average crypto user it is hard for them to rely on many pieces of technology for different functionalities. Having everything centralized makes it much more ideal for the average user, which is what Omni is striving to provide. We're obviously very early, but if this starts getting adopted, the potential is insanely high. The community here is goated too.

comment.comment: OMNI is taking crypto privacy to an entirely different level by building a comprehensive privacy ecosystem rather than simply another private transaction protocol. Its technology combines zero knowledge proofs, locally generated and encrypted private keys, confidential computing, private payments, and a Quantum Safe Vault designed to protect assets against future quantum computing threats. One of its biggest advantages over Nullmask is its approach to self custody and financial privacy: OMNI is designed so the team cannot access your private keys or see your private balance, whereas Nullmask explicitly acknowledges that its servers can access users private balances and transaction histories. OMNI is also expanding privacy into AI, confidential data processing, and broader blockchain infrastructure. Ultimately, OMNI isn't just trying to hide transactions; it's working toward an ecosystem where your assets, financial activity, identity, and information remain under your control. Mind you we are still in the beta building phase, and the tek works. Upside is extraordinary.
